html:
The Duchy of Milan was a state in Lombardy, the rich plain of northern Italy, centred on the city of Milan, from 1395 to 1797. The map shows it from 1530 to 1715, when Spain and then Austria ruled it.

The Visconti lords of Milan bought the title of duke from the emperor in 1395. In 1450 the soldier Francesco Sforza took over, and the Sforza court became one of the brightest of the Renaissance. Ludovico Sforza employed Leonardo da Vinci, who painted The Last Supper in a Milan convent.

Milan's wealth and its place on the roads over the Alps made it the great prize of the Italian Wars, and French and imperial armies fought over it for decades. When the last Sforza died in 1535, the emperor Charles V took it, and it stayed with Spain for nearly two centuries. Austria took it during the War of the Spanish Succession. Napoleon ended the duchy in 1797, and after 1815 it was part of Austrian Lombardy.
